title: Stop the checkout doing work it then throws away

blocks.text: The checkout looks up the customer by email and the price of every item before it takes payment. Since the last release the customer table grows by one row on every visit of a returning customer, and the bill for the catalogue service shows one call per item in every basket, as if the price cache weren't there.

Finish `customerId(...)` and `price(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Checkout.java`. When you're done, a customer's row is inserted on their first visit only, and the catalogue is asked for each SKU once, after which the cache answers. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a first-time customer gets exactly one new row, and its id is returned
an uncached price is fetched from the catalogue once and cached
a returning customer gets their existing id and no row is inserted
a cached price is answered without calling the catalogue

origin.section: Every Argument Is Evaluated, Left to Right, Before the Method Runs

concepts: Every argument is evaluated before the method runs, whether or not the method uses it, so work that may not be needed is passed as a Supplier or a function.
